problem: State-of-the-art image-based RL agents (CURL, RAD, DreamerV2, MWM) generalize poorly out-of-distribution (unseen scenes and textures) in iGibson PointGoal navigation, and prior language-conditioned RL (Voltron, Dynalang) only grounds vision in language implicitly.
motivation: Language is discrete and captures high-level concepts and global context, which should help OoD and sim-to-real generalization. Vision-language foundation models are too resource hungry for edge robots, so the paper asks whether language can improve a lightweight image-based world model.
key_idea: Mask object bounding boxes in the RGB observation and give a templated language description of the masked objects to a masked autoencoder, so that reconstruction of the masked regions forces language-grounded visual features for a Dreamer-style world model.
insight: Language grounding only helps when it is enforced explicitly. The ablation shows that removing the language descriptions (empty text at train time) or removing object masking drops LanGWM to MWM level (Env Avg SR 1.5 and 1.7 vs 6.8). Both components are therefore necessary and complementary. The gain over MWM and data-augmented DreamerV2 is modest in absolute terms, and a Grounding-DINO variant (37.1 SR) remains far stronger.
method: Object instance masking: randomly pick up to 3 objects per RGB frame (stopping at 75% of the image masked) and mask their bounding boxes with a random 0-10 px margin. Spatial jitter, Gaussian blur, color jitter and grayscale augmentations are also applied.

Language description generation: template sentences built from the object's semantic class, horizontal direction (left/front/right or 5-way) and distance, e.g. 'If you look {distance} in the {direction}, you will see {object}'. Seven templates and two direction rules are used.

Language-grounded MAE: early conv layers give visual tokens, which are randomly masked at 75% (MWM style). They are concatenated with frozen BERT-base embeddings (20 tokens + 1 pooled token) and passed to a ViT encoder. The language tokens are sliced out before the decoder so the decoder cannot cheat. The decoder reconstructs depth (RGB input, depth target) and reward with an MSE loss.
Inference without language: at evaluation, empty-description constant tokens are given, so BERT is used only for training and depth is only a training signal.
World model: DreamerV2-style RSSM with discrete latents (32x32), representation and predictive transition models and a KL loss, built on top of the MAE features.

Controller: actor-critic trained in imagination, with imagination horizon 15. MAE features and task observations (goal, pose, velocities) are concatenated and pooled with a small transformer autoencoder before entering the controller. The MAE, world model and controller are optimized separately.
Implementation: built on the DreamerV2 and MWM code bases; about 2 days of training on 2x RTX 3090 for 100k steps.

setting.backbone: MAE ViT (4 enc / 3 dec layers) + frozen BERT-base (train only) + DreamerV2 RSSM + actor-critic, trained from scratch
setting.model_size: BERT 110M frozen; the rest is small (256-dim transformer)
setting.training_data: 100k environment interaction steps in iGibson 1.0 on 12 training scenes with training textures; templated language from GT semantic instance masks; depth as reconstruction target
setting.observation: RGB (128x160) + task observations (goal location, current location, linear/angular velocity); depth only for training
setting.action_space: continuous (rotation in radians, forward distance in meters), TurtleBot
setting.privileged: Ground-truth instance masks, semantic classes and depth are used for training only; none at test time (empty language).

numbers.eval_set_note: Held-out 3 scenes (Ihlen_0_int, Ihlen_1_int, Rs_int) plus held-out textures; average of 3 seeds; 100k training steps
numbers.backbone: Object-masked MAE with BERT language + DreamerV2 world model
numbers.extra: 100k interaction steps; GT masks/depth/semantics used in training only
numbers.evidence: Table 1, LanGWM row, Env Avg (SR 6.8, SPL 0.04); per-scene SR 8.3 / 2.1 / 9.9

numbers.backbone: same, no object mask and no language

numbers_note: Benchmark is iGibson 1.0 PointGoal with a custom OoD split (5 train scenes stated in text vs 12 listed in appendix; 3 test scenes), not a canonical benchmark. SR is printed in percent, SPL as a fraction. Also reported in the table: the DreamerV2 + Grounding DINO reference row (SR 37.1) is a baseline, not included.
results: LanGWM reaches Env Avg SR 6.8 / SPL 0.04 at 100k steps, beating DreamerV2 + data augmentation (5.5), CURL (4.7), MWM (1.7), DreamerV2 (1.3) and RAD (0.5). SPL is tied with CURL and DreamerV2+DA at 0.04. It remains far below the Grounding-DINO-augmented DreamerV2 (37.1 SR).
limitations: Absolute success rates are very low (under 10%) and gains over the baselines are small; SPL is not improved over CURL or DreamerV2+DA.

Language descriptions are templated from ground-truth instance/semantic/depth information available in simulation, and only a single benchmark is evaluated, with no real-robot or sim-to-real experiments.
Performance is far below a Grounding-DINO foundation-model variant; the claim of human-robot interaction potential is not tested.
